newsitem.title: INDIA: India allows export 50,000 t coarse grains, flour.
newsitem.headline: India allows export 50,000 t coarse grains, flour.

text.p: The Indian government announced on Wednesday it had authorised the export of an additional 50,000 tonnes of coarse grains and flour during the 1996/97 (April-March) financial year.

The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) said in a notice published in the Economic Times newspaper that only public sector undertakings were eligible to export the coarse grains and flour.
It said the public sector undertakings could be at the state or federal level and could include cooperative federations.
The notice said the grains and flour included barley, maize, yellow hybrid maize of cattle feed quality, bajra and ragi. Also included was jowar, excluding hybrid jowar grown as kharif crop, it said.
An APEDA official told Reuters the 50,000-tonne tranche came on top of an earlier 50,000 tonnes, which were authorised in April and May for export during the 1996/97 fiscal year.
APEDA said it issued a trade notice on Monday spelling out procedures for issuance of Registration-Cum-Allocation-Certificates, or licences.
The first allocation of the export quota will be made from applications received up to 3:00 p.m. (0930 GMT) on November 29, it said.
